newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines Dec money levels below IMF ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Philippines Dec money levels below IMF ceiling.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Monday that base money and reserve money levels in December were 15 billion pesos below a ceiling set by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"Latest Central Bank preliminary data show that in December, the Central Bank's operating targets on BM (base money) and RM (reserve money) were more than 15.0 billon pesos below programmed ceilings," the bank said in a statement.
The bank did not disclose the actual levels of both base and reserve money.

However, it said the annual growth rate of base money slowed down to 14.1 percent in December from 18.1 percent in June, while reserve money expanded by only 15.7 percent in December as compared with 18.3 percent in June.
The Central Bank attributed the slowdown in monetary growth to its aggressive open market operations and coordination with the government regarding withdrawal of its funds out of the Central Bank.

Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson added that the slowdown was a major factor in keeping inflation in December well below the projected 6.5 percent. Inflation was an annualised 5.1 prcent in the month.

Base money includes money in circulation, reserve balances and government securities deposited with the central bank and the aggregate reserve deficiencies of banks. Reserve money is base money minus the governments securities deposited with the central bank.
"In step with the performance of BM and RM, the Central Bank governor added that domestic liquidity (M3) ... was more than 50 billion pesos below the indicative ceiling," the statement added.
Domestic liquidity is base money plus deposits and deposit substitutes of banks.
Domestic liquidity is base money plus deposits and banks' deposit substitutes.

"The central bank shall continue to rely on open market operations as needed and continue to closely coordinate with the National Government to contain any unnecessary injection of additional funds into the system," Singson said.
In a separate statement, IMF resident representative David Nellor lauded the relatively low inflation rate, saying it "helps establish a favourable macroeconomic environment for 1997".
